opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices and running the company. Grew slower than revenue — $1,354M vs $1,221M a year ago.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new turbines, grid and energy-transition technology — about $0.4B in the quarter as reported in the release narrative.

footerNote: Gross profit is shown as $3,106M (revenue less reported costs) so the lines add up exactly; the release rounds it to $3,107M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue of $12.6B, up from $10.0B a year ago; +18% organically, led by Power and Electrification

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up from $1.64 a year ago; net income was $1.3B, a 10.2% margin

kpis.label: Backlog
kpis.note: Orders of $29.3B in the quarter, +96% organically; backlog grew $20B in three months

kpis.label: Electrification revenue
kpis.note: +51% as reported (+16% organically) — grid equipment is booming, helped by the Prolec GE acquisition

oneTimers: Separation costs of $31M (from the spin-out from GE) and restructuring charges of $6M were excluded from adjusted EBITDA of $1,943M.
GE Vernova paid about $350M in the quarter to transfer part of its retiree benefit obligations to an insurer, which took over legal and administrative responsibility for them.
The company resolved all outstanding litigation over the Vineyard Wind offshore project in Massachusetts.
otherDetail: Other income of $388M is made up of $71M of interest and other financial income, $212M of non-operating benefit income (pension and retiree-benefit plans), and $105M of other income — net. That $105M includes $31M of equity-method investment income, $35M of gains on purchases and sales of business interests, $21M from derivatives, $7M of net interest and investment income, $4M of licensing income and $6M of other items (components total $104M; $1M rounding in the filing).

segments.name: Power
segments.note: Gas turbines and other power-plant equipment and services — the biggest business. Revenue +25% on heavy-duty and aeroderivative turbine deliveries; gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations reached 122 GW.

segments.name: Electrification
segments.note: Grid equipment — substations, transformers and high-voltage gear that move electricity. Revenue +51% as reported, including Prolec GE; +16% organically.

segments.name: Wind
segments.note: Wind turbines, onshore and offshore, plus servicing. Revenue +4%, and the segment swung to a small $72M EBITDA profit from a $61M loss a year ago.

segments.name: Other/eliminations
segments.note: Other revenues minus sales between GE Vernova's own segments, removed so the segments add up to the company total.

takeaways.text: Orders rose 96% organically to $29.3B, driven by Power equipment, and total backlog grew $20B in one quarter to $197B. Gas Power equipment backlog plus slot reservation agreements rose from 116 GW to 122 GW, and the company now expects at least 130 GW under contract by year-end 2026.
takeaways.title: Orders nearly doubled

takeaways.text: Electrification revenue jumped 51% to $3.9B (+16% without the Prolec GE acquisition) as utilities buy substations and transmission gear, while Power revenue rose 25% to $6.1B. Electrification equipment backlog reached $42.2B, up 60% in a year.
takeaways.title: Grid gear is the growth star

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $5.4B, up from $732M a year ago, lifting the cash balance to $16.8B. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $46.5–$47.5B of revenue and $16–$17B of free cash flow, and the board lifted the share-buyback authorization to $20B.
takeaways.title: Cash poured in, guidance went up

verdict: GE Vernova had a very strong quarter — sales jumped 27% to $12.6B as surging demand for gas turbines and grid equipment swelled orders to $29.3B and the backlog to $197B, producing $1.3B of profit.
